clue.text: Married woman is hard and not feminine

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A description of a wife who is tough and unladylike.
explanation.definitionFit: Mannish describes a woman with traits thought typical of a man, so lacking femininity.

clue.text: Latin master's upset — head of school reads Sallust wrongly?

indicators.note: the words Latin master's are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
the possessive s counts as a letter here

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word school is taken

explanation.surface: A Latin teacher is upset that the headmaster misreads a Roman historian.
explanation.walkthrough: Sallust was a Roman historian, standard school Latin; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the meaning of a Latin author wrong is one instance of rendering a text incorrectly.

clue.text: Being aware about husband's love

indicators.note: the awareness word goes around the husband letter

parts.note: noting means observing or being aware of

explanation.surface: Knowing all about a husband's love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis love means a score of zero, nil.

clue.text: Country full of life but not very wealthy ultimately

indicators.note: the very letter is dropped from the lively word

parts.note: vital means lively, full of life

indicators.note: the last letter of the word wealthy is used

explanation.surface: A lively nation that is not so rich in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a country in southern Europe.

clue.text: Spooner's man risky in prayer

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two sounds trade places

parts.note: a male is a man
hairy is slang for dangerous or risky

explanation.surface: A dangerous man caught praying.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of MALE HAIRY gives HAIL MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is a Catholic prayer to the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: China has very good football team

parts.note: china (plate) is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so a pal
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A Chinese side contains an excellent football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is rhyming slang: china plate = mate. Crystal Palace is a London football club, usually just called Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Palace is the everyday short name of Crystal Palace, a London football club.

clue.text: State a religious observance that's good for church

indicators.note: the good letter stands in for the church letters

parts.note: penance is a religious act of contrition
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A statement that a religious observance is good for the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb but is the definition; 'for' puts G in place of CE in PENANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Penang is a state of Malaysia.

clue.text: Graceful home is let out

indicators.note: the letters of home is let are put out of their order

explanation.surface: An elegant house is available to rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithesome, a variant of lissom, means supple and graceful.

clue.text: Top fighting force with fashionable leader

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: An elite army unit with a stylish commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain leads a team or ship, so is a leader.

clue.text: One in office having got hold of university post

indicators.note: the combined word grips the university letter within it
the numeral one is placed inside the word for office

parts.note: a station is a position or office someone holds
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An official who has secured a job at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside STATION, giving SITATION; that then takes U inside after SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a job or position, as in 'situations vacant', so a post.

clue.text: Strike by journalist put on record

parts.note: to tap is to strike lightly
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist hit someone and the incident was documented.
explanation.definitionFit: Taped means recorded on tape, hence put on record.

clue.text: Stall with monster fish enthralling the woman

parts.note: a dragon is a mythical monster

indicators.note: the fish word captures the woman word within it

parts.note: eels are fish
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A market stall with a monstrous fish holding a woman spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' looks like a market booth, but it is the verb, to delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag one's heels is to delay deliberately, to stall.

clue.text: Clever bishop turned out to be wet

indicators.note: the bishop is thrown out of the word for clever

parts.note: brainy means clever
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A smart bishop proved to be feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like 'proved', but it evicts B from BRAINY. 'Wet' also tempts as 'feeble', a British sense, but here it means rain-soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainy weather is wet weather, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Native American woman sounds like a bit of a laugh

indicators.note: signals that the answer is said the same as the phrase for a small laugh

parts.note: a small laugh would be a mini ha-ha

explanation.surface: A tribal woman whose name sounds faintly amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: Minnehaha is the heroine of Longfellow's poem The Song of Hiawatha.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Dakota woman beloved of Hiawatha in Longfellow's poem.

clue.text: A piece written about politician is worthless

indicators.note: the phrase is written the other way about, i.e. backwards

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun, so a piece is a gun
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An article written about a politician is of no value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like an article but is gun slang; 'written about' reverses A GUN to NUGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory is a formal word for trifling or of no value.

clue.text: One side in war agrees to limit explosive

indicators.note: the agreeing word bounds the explosive within it

parts.note: tallies means agrees or corresponds
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: A warring faction agrees to restrict explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: In both World Wars the Allies were one of the two opposing camps.

clue.text: Carried round island

parts.note: borne is the past participle of bear, to carry
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone was transported around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia.

clue.text: The bad deed not half looking dreadful towards the end

indicators.note: only half of the word deed, its first two letters, is used
dreadful-looking letters are in a mess, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked act seems even worse as it nears its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps DE; with THEBAD, 'looking dreadful' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: On one's deathbed means close to dying, near the end of life.

clue.text: Philosopher takes time to present a case

parts.note: John Locke was an English philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher needs a while to argue his point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present a case' reads as making an argument; the case is a small container.
explanation.definitionFit: A locket is a small hinged case worn on a chain, holding a picture or hair.

clue.text: Take remedy suitable for swallowing

indicators.note: the remedy word swallows the suitable word

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
apt means suitable

explanation.surface: Instructions to take a medicine that is meant to be swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture is to take, as in seizing a prisoner or a piece.

clue.text: Always taking time to get to front of bar for drink

indicators.note: the always-plus-time pair comes after the bar letter
the first letter of the word bar is used

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone forever slow to reach the bar for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water.

clue.text: Sailor's stuck on guard, for a change

indicators.note: the letters of on guard are changed around

explanation.surface: A sailor stuck on sentry duty for a change.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has run aground is stuck on the bottom, a nautical sense.

clue.text: African city commander, a little short of terrible

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman commander

indicators.note: the terrible word loses a little, its last letter

parts.note: dire means terrible

explanation.surface: A commander in an African city falls not far short of terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a port city in Morocco.

clue.text: Excellent work by female, new person in driving seat in firm?

indicators.note: the three short pieces sit inside the word for firm

parts.note: tight means firm or secure
OP is short for opus, a work
a learner driver displays an L plate

explanation.surface: Praise for a woman's work and a new boss at a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but gives TIGHT. L is the learner plate on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest rank or quality, hence excellent.

clue.text: What angler may catch with rod

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish caught on a line
an old unit of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole

explanation.surface: A fish caught on a fishing rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rod' reads as the angler's tackle, but it is the old length measure, equal to five and a half yards.
explanation.definitionFit: Perch is both a common freshwater fish and the old unit of length also called a rod or pole.

clue.text: What's terrible pain beginning to cause maybe?

definitions.text: What's terrible pain beginning to cause maybe?

indicators.note: pain made terrible is reshaped into a new order
the first letter of the word cause is taken

explanation.surface: Asking what severe pain might start to bring on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: terrible pain may well cause sudden alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic, sudden overwhelming fear, is one thing terrible pain may bring about.

clue.text: Arab Spring's beginning with a declaration of independence

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Spring is taken

parts.note: UDI is a unilateral declaration of independence, as Rhodesia made in 1965

explanation.surface: The Arab Spring opened with a nation declaring independence.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saudi is a native of Saudi Arabia, so an Arab.

clue.text: Security of tenure foolishly given to backward-looking educationist

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the educationist is read from right to left

parts.note: a BEd (Bachelor of Education) holder is a trained teacher

indicators.note: the word tenure is scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Job security given unwisely to a reactionary teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward-looking' turns BED into DEB; 'foolishly' rearranges TENURE into ENTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A debenture is a bond issued by a company, a kind of financial security.

clue.text: Report of official controller that could provide a smokescreen

indicators.note: a report is a sound, so the controller's title is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a censor officially controls what may be published

explanation.surface: News of an official who might be hiding the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smokescreen' suggests a cover-up; the smoke is literal incense.
explanation.definitionFit: A censer is a vessel burning incense in church, so it gives off a screen of smoke.

clue.text: Fixes a day for murder at the end of the month

indicators.note: the murder day follows the month abbreviation

parts.note: Dec is short for December
Julius Caesar was murdered on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: Someone sets a date for a killing late in the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of the month' suggests the last days; instead IDES is placed at the end of DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide something is to settle or fix it.
